Subject: Follow-up from today — compliance & admin events

Hi Rishi / Lauren,

Thanks for taking the time today — good conversation. I wanted to capture the questions we walked through so our security team can prioritize. High level items:

- SOC 2 status: you mentioned Redwood is in the middle of Type II; can you confirm scope (in-scope services) and estimated report date?
- GDPR / HIPAA: we are scoped for HIPAA; need confirmation that PHI is segregated and whether Redwood offers BAAs.
- Vendor security questionnaire: attached the MedixCorp supplier questionnaire (PDF) — please confirm who will lead responses and rough ETA.
- Audit logging / admin events: specifics requested by our security team:
  - Which admin actions are logged (user provisioning, permission changes, role assignments, key rotations, model pinning, route changes)?
  - Are API-level request events available (requester identity, endpoint, request/response size, latency)?
  - Exportability: can logs be exported programmatically (push to customer S3, pull + bulk export) and in what formats (JSONL, Parquet)?
  - Retention and immutability: do you support append-only or WORM-style retention (S3 Object Lock, write-once ledger) and can retention be customer-controlled?

We also have two practical asks:
1) a short artifacts pack (SOC 2 status note + sample admin-event schema + export runbook) to share with our internal auditors; and
2) schedule a technical deep-dive with an engineer to confirm the export and immutability design (we prefer an APAC-friendly time, but have flexibility).

I've attached the questionnaire to this thread. Let me know who on your side should own the response and if sharing a short artifact bundle by EOD Friday (PST) is reasonable.

Best,
Alex Chen
Security & Compliance — MedixCorp
alex.chen@medixcorp.com

- HIPAA / BAA: we support HIPAA customers and offer a BAA; I will loop in Legal if Medix wants a draft.
- Ownership: Stephanie Nguyen (cc'd on this thread) will own the technical side of the vendor questionnaire and the admin-event artifact. I'll own coordination and the SOC/contract pieces.
- Artifact pack: we can provide a short ZIP containing: SOC status note, admin-activity-exports-overview.pdf (overview + runbook), and a sample JSONL of admin events. ETA: Friday EOB PST is reasonable — we will aim for earlier.
- Technical deep dive: please pick a time on my calendly (link below) or suggest 11/12 or 11/15 in the morning PST. Stephanie will do the deep-dive.

Additional clarifications on export/immutability we can confirm with Stephanie: push vs pull exports, support for S3 Object Lock vs internal immutable ledger, retention configuration per customer, and export SLA (typical 24–72 hour on-demand bulk exports, streaming/push near-real-time).

I attached a short overview PDF that should help answer a number of the logging questions; Stephanie will follow up with a sample schema and a stub export flow.

Thanks —

Hi Alex — Stephanie from Redwood infra/security engineering. Thanks for the detailed list — below are concrete answers and what I'll include in the sample artifact.

1) Events captured (non-exhaustive):
   - Authentication events: login success/failure, MFA enrollment, SSO assertions (user id, idp, timestamp)
   - Admin actions: user create/update/delete, role/permission changes, policy updates, service account key rotations, model deployment/pin/unpin, route changes, canary/rollout events
   - API request traces: request_id, caller_identity (redacted where required), endpoint, method, request_size_bytes, response_size_bytes, latency_ms, status_code, timestamp
   - System events: autoscale events, node allocation, certificate rotations

2) Schema & format: primary export format is newline-delimited JSON (JSONL). We can also provide Parquet on request (batch export). Sample fields in the JSONL will be included in sample-admin-events.jsonl (attached).

3) Export mechanisms:
   - Push: We can deliver events to a customer-managed S3 bucket via signed role OR via secure HTTPS webhook (near-real-time).
   - Pull/Bulk: On-demand bulk export (ZIP/Parquet/JSONL) from console or via API. Typical SLA for bulk export is 24–72 hours depending on window size.

4) Immutability & retention:
   - Customer-controlled retention windows are supported. We offer two immutability options:
     a) S3 Object Lock (governance/compliance mode) for customer-managed S3 exports.
     b) Append-only internal ledger for hosted storage — exports of ledger can be signed and time-stamped.
   - We do not currently provide WORM appliances on-prem by default, but for Dedicated/Private deployments we can enable stricter write-once configs as part of the deployment plan.

5) Access controls & proof:
   - Export logs include signed metadata (hash and timestamp) so you can validate export integrity.
   - We maintain audit trails for export operations (who requested, when, destination).

Deliverables I'll attach / share in the artifact pack: sample-admin-events.jsonl (first 100 events), export runbook (steps: configure target S3 role, set retention, request bulk export), and a short note on verification (how to validate hashes).

Next steps I propose:
- I will upload the artifact pack to the HubSpot deal and share a link here by EOD PST Friday.
- Schedule a 30m technical deep-dive — I can cover export config, IAM setup, and immutability verification.

If you have specific fields you need in the JSONL, call them out and I will include them (for example, include full request payload redaction policy).

Regards,
Stephanie Nguyen
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
